root_cause.text: In `iommu_sva_unbind_device()`, the IOMMU SVA teardown used `domain->mm->iommu_mm` after calling `iommu_domain_free(domain)`, even though freeing the domain can drop and free the associated `mm` via `mmdrop()/__mmdrop()/mm_pasid_drop()`, causing a use-after-free of the `mm` structure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that "`domain->mm->iommu_mm` can be freed by `iommu_domain_free()`" and that "After `iommu_domain_free()` returns, accessing `domain->mm->iommu_mm` may dereference a freed mm structure"; correspondingly, the patch moves the `list_empty(&iommu_mm->sva_domains)` / `list_del(&iommu_mm->mm_list_elm)` logic to before `iommu_domain_free(domain)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix iommu SVA unbind cleanup so mm list removal and presence flag updates occur only when the last domain user is released.
intent_record.what: The code moves the check for an empty iommu_mm->sva_domains list, the removal of iommu_mm->mm_list_elm from the global list, and the update of iommu_sva_present under the condition that --domain->users == 0, placing these operations before iommu_domain_free(domain) inside that block instead of executing them unconditionally afterward.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cleanup of the per-mm SVA domain list membership and the global presence flag now happens only when the last user of the domain is removed and the domain is being deleted, preventing the code from treating iommu_mm as having no active SVA domains during unbinds where the domain still has remaining users.

grouping_result.intent: Fix iommu SVA unbind cleanup so mm list removal and presence flag updates occur only when the last domain user is released.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets iommu_sva_unbind_device() teardown ordering/lifetime by deferring mm list removal and presence flag updates until the last domain reference is released, which directly addresses the mm use-after-free caused when domain free can also free the associated mm.
